pylon_custom.description: Inverted Y with a DIAMOND foot. Two straight, heavy legs come down from a long single head, splay outward and pass just outside the deck edges, where a cross-beam carries the deck. Below the deck they converge INWARD to a footing ≈0.55 × the leg spread at the deck, leaving an arched opening under the deck beam. The legs merge ≈40% of the above-deck height (≈56 m); the tapered single head (≈60%) carries a dense fan of stays in two planes.

model3d.notes: Shape read from Commons photos (pylon close-up from the deck; tower under construction 2007, which shows the A-frame legs and the under-deck strut). Height 175.3 m total (mageba), of which ≈135 m above deck. Side-span auxiliary piers at 40 m spacing (2×40 m end spans). Stays fan from the single head to both deck edges. Steel box girder in the main span, concrete in the side spans. Pass 2 (2026-11-26): corrected from the client's sunset photo and Commons side views (Anh Khoa 32866753646 / 32907235505): below the deck the legs converge to a narrower footing (diamond), not an A-frame splay. Merge ≈56 m above deck (≈40%, measured on photos 21 and 24: head ≈57–62% of the above-deck height); head ≈79 m. Auxiliary piers at 40 and 80 m from each unit end (2 × 40 m end spans); unit length 930 m, so 850/890 from the start. Steel box main span. Review r1: Aux piers at 930/970 m (unit 1010 m); 27 stays per side per plane (216 stays); custom pylon scaled to 175.3 m total.

notes: Span arrangement 210 + 450 + 210 m (main span 450 m) from the contractor page (Bắc Trung Nam), adopted by client decision 2026-11-26; replaces the earlier 350 m client estimate. Known: TEDI–BR design PM02 won the architectural competition (HCMC decision, 4/2026); cable-stayed main bridge ≈870 m with 2 symmetric pylons, 2 cable planes, steel–concrete composite girder, deck ≈33.5 m, 8 lanes; navigation channel 250 × 55 m (Ministry of Construction, channel shifted ≈340 m toward Đồng Nai). Route ≈6.3 km (4.6 km HCMC, 1.7 km Đồng Nai) from Nguyễn Hữu Thọ (Nhà Bè) to Liên Cảng – 25C (Đại Phước). Groundbreaking 15/1/2026 (taken as construction_start); completion target 2029. COORDINATES APPROXIMATE (on the Nhà Bè river between Nhà Bè and Đại Phước).
